# Task P1-05: Album-policy engine

**Phase:** 1 · **Depends on:** P1-01 (enums), P1-03 (`VersionFlags`) · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
Every song gets exactly one album context, chosen by the library's album policy (`LIBRARY_OUTPUT.md` §7.3): `fewest_albums` (the Plexamp default — the smallest set of real releases that hold ≥ 2 owned tracks each, everything else in the artist's "Singles" pseudo-album), `singles_only`, `original_album`, `single_release` and `compilation`. Assignments are **sticky**: planning a batch of new songs never moves an existing song, it can only join existing albums or create new ones. The engine is pure (no I/O); the song-add service (P1-07) feeds it and persists the result. Behaviour is pinned by `tests/fixtures/album-policy.json`.

## Rules
**Eligibility** of an option for a song (every policy): `Status` is `Official` (case-insensitive); `PrimaryType` is Album, EP or Single; `SecondaryTypes` is empty — except that `Live` is allowed when the song has the `Live` flag and `Remix`/`DJ-mix` when it has `Remix`. Compilations, soundtracks, promos, bootlegs, broadcasts are never chosen.

**Kind** of a real album: Album → `Album`, EP → `Ep`, Single → `Single`. Title, album artist, date, release/group ids come from the chosen option; `TrackNo`, `DiscNo` (default 1), `TotalTracks` from the option; `OriginalDate` is always the song's own.

**Joining an existing album** (every policy except `singles_only` and `compilation`): a song joins an existing non-pseudo album of **its artist** when one of its eligible options has `Key == AlbumKey` or the same non-null `MbReleaseGroupId`. It then takes the existing album's key, title, album artist, date and ids, and track/disc/total from the matching option (exact key preferred over same group). Several candidates → the one with the most tracks, then earliest date, then key ordinal.

**`FewestAlbums`**, per artist (artists in order of first appearance):
1. join existing albums as above;
2. greedy set cover over the remaining songs: count, per option `Key`, how many remaining songs have it as an eligible option; take the best (most songs → Album before EP before Single → earliest `Date`, nulls last → `Key` ordinal) if it covers ≥ `MinTracksPerRealAlbum`, assign those songs, repeat; stop when the best covers fewer;
3. the rest go to the artist's pseudo-album.

**`OriginalAlbum`**: per song, after trying to join an existing album, the eligible Album/EP option with the earliest `ReleaseGroupFirstDate ?? Date` (then Album before EP, then `Date`, then key); none → the `SingleRelease` rule; none → pseudo-album.
**`SingleRelease`**: the eligible Single with the earliest `ReleaseGroupFirstDate ?? Date`; none → the `OriginalAlbum` rule; none → pseudo-album. (Joining existing albums happens first here too.)
**`SinglesOnly`**: every song goes to its artist's pseudo-album.
**`Compilation`**: every song goes to the library's single `Various Artists` album: the existing album with `Kind == Compilation && IsVariousArtists`, else a new one (`AlbumTitle` = `LibraryName`, `AlbumArtist` = "Various Artists", `Kind` Compilation, `IsVariousArtists` true, no release ids).

**Pseudo-album** (`Kind` PseudoSingles, `AlbumTitle` "Singles", `AlbumArtist` = the artist's name, no release ids, `DiscNo` 1, `TotalTracks` null): the artist's existing pseudo-album if there is one (its key and date), otherwise a new key from `newGuid()` (allocated when first needed, in processing order) with `Date` = the earliest 4-digit year among the `OriginalDate`s of the songs that land in it in this batch (null if none). Track numbers continue after the existing album's `MaxTrackNo` (0 when new) in input order. The new compilation album follows the same date and numbering rules.

- Pure and deterministic: no I/O, no clock, no `Guid.NewGuid()` except through the injected delegate. No new packages. Use `StringComparer.Ordinal` for key ordering.
- Deserialize the fixture with `System.Text.Json` (camelCase, `JsonStringEnumConverter`, a converter for `VersionFlags` from a wire-name array).
